findings.statement: CXCR2 tops the convergence ranking: pooled UC-vs-control log2FC [gene=CXCR2; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=2.814], up in all eight cohorts, with Open Targets genetic association and clinical-stage antagonists (navarixin, reparixin, ladarixin). Within patients the gain is local to inflamed mucosa (paired inflamed vs non-inflamed log2FC [gene=CXCR2; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=inflamed_vs_noninflamed_paired; log2fc=1.6972]) and only small in non-inflamed mucosa [gene=CXCR2; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=noninflamed_vs_control; log2fc=0.6399]. CXCR2 is a neutrophil receptor, so the bulk signal largely reflects neutrophil infiltration (cell-context specialist to confirm).

CXCL8, the ligand of CXCR1 and CXCR2, is strongly and reproducibly up (pooled log2FC [gene=CXCL8; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=3.864], eight of eight cohorts) and enriched in inflamed mucosa of the same patient (paired log2FC [gene=CXCL8; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=inflamed_vs_noninflamed_paired; log2fc=1.968]). It has no genetic support in the ranking; the axis rests on expression, literature and drug history, and the signal is neutrophil-recruitment driven.

MMP3 is among the largest pooled increases (log2FC [gene=MMP3; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=4.9012]) and is up in all eight cohorts. It is local to inflamed mucosa (paired log2FC [gene=MMP3; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=inflamed_vs_noninflamed_paired; log2fc=2.3368]), which makes it a tissue-inflammation marker. MMP1, MMP7 and MMP10 behave the same way; broad MMP inhibitors (marimastat) have no genetic support here.

HMGCS2, an epithelial ketogenesis/metabolism gene, is lost in UC (pooled log2FC [gene=HMGCS2; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=-3.8375]), significantly down in all eight cohorts. The loss is restricted to inflamed mucosa: in non-inflamed mucosa of MSCCR it is unchanged from controls [gene=HMGCS2; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=noninflamed_vs_control; log2fc=-0.0649]. It is a marker of local inflammation, not a target.

DUOX2, an epithelial source of reactive oxygen species, is strongly up (pooled log2FC [gene=DUOX2; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=4.4116]) in all eight cohorts. Its increase is mostly inflamed-specific, with a small but significant rise in non-inflamed mucosa [gene=DUOX2; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=noninflamed_vs_control; log2fc=0.8129], so part of it may reflect the disease state rather than current inflammation. The heterogeneity across cohorts is high, so effect sizes should not be compared between cohorts. It has no genetic support or approved drug.

REG1A has a large pooled increase (log2FC [gene=REG1A; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=4.4862]) but is less reproducible than the leading genes: significant in six of eight cohorts, and not significant in the Leuven GSE16879 cohort (padj [gene=REG1A; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE16879; layer=rna; cohort=GSE16879; contrast=uc_vs_control; padj=0.132]) or the adult colon GSE165512 cohort, even though the direction is up in both. It is a strong biomarker candidate with a caveat on sample size and variance.

JAK2 has the strongest genetic and tractability support in the ranking but only a modest expression change (pooled log2FC [gene=JAK2; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=0.874]), significant in all eight cohorts. Its rank therefore comes from genetics and drugs (JAK inhibitors), not from a large expression change. The change is partly inflammation-local.

AQP8 shows the largest pooled loss in UC (log2FC [gene=AQP8; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=-5.246]), significant down in seven of eight cohorts. Together with CLDN8, SLC26A2, PCK1, GUCA2A/B and UGT2A3, it forms a reproducible epithelial absorptive, barrier and metabolism loss signature, a biomarker set that is not a target set.

S100A8 (with S100A9 and S100A12) is strongly up (pooled log2FC [gene=S100A8; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=4.7697]) in all eight cohorts. These are neutrophil and monocyte calprotectin genes, so the bulk rise mainly reflects infiltrating myeloid cells and not a change inside epithelium; the cell-context specialist should confirm it with single-cell data. It has no genetic support.

IDO1 is strongly and consistently up (pooled log2FC [gene=IDO1; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=3.118]) in all eight cohorts. It has inhibitors in phase 3 and approval-stage records (from oncology), but no genetic evidence, and the rise may be partly interferon-driven by immune cells.

CD274 (PD-L1) is up in all eight cohorts (pooled log2FC [gene=CD274; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=1.974]) and has genetic association and literature support, pointing to an interferon-responsive checkpoint program in inflamed mucosa. The target direction is unclear: the data support an adaptive brake, so checkpoint agonism, not blockade, would be the logical direction, and this is not shown by expression.

SLC26A3, a chloride/bicarbonate exchanger with genetic association to UC, is down (pooled log2FC [gene=SLC26A3; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=-1.702]) in all eight cohorts. It is a rare example of a lost epithelial gene with genetic support, so it is a mechanism and biomarker candidate. Any therapy would need to restore function, since the gene is already reduced.

caveats: Pooled log2FC values come from a random-effects model with very high heterogeneity for most top genes, so effect sizes are less reliable than direction and significance.
Microarray cohorts (UNIFI, PURSUIT, Leuven) have compressed fold changes compared with RNA-seq; compare direction and significance, not size.

Bulk biopsies are rich in infiltrating neutrophils and myeloid cells; the increases of CXCR1/2, CXCL8, S100A8/9/12, IL1B, TREM1 and LCN2 probably come mainly from those cells. This needs the cell-context specialist's single-cell and composition check.
Paired inflamed vs non-inflamed and non-inflamed vs control contrasts exist only in the MSCCR cohort.
Genes with high rank but zero genetics (CXCL8, IDO1, MMPs) rely on literature and drug history from other diseases; expression alone does not show that a target is causal or safe.
